questions.q: Why can't a technical architect operate the way a specialist developer does, going deep in just one area?
options: Because Salesforce certifications forbid specialization
Because the architect role is defined by breadth across every domain that affects a solution's integrity
Because developers are not allowed to talk to architects
Because depth in one domain is never useful at all
questions.explain: A developer can excel by going deep in one area; an architect's defining skill is being capable enough across every relevant domain to catch cross-domain problems, even without being the deepest specialist in any single one.

questions.q: Which domain is specifically about who a user is and how that identity is established and trusted across systems?
options: Data architecture
Development lifecycle and deployment
Identity and access management
Integration architecture
questions.explain: Identity and access management covers establishing and trusting who a user actually is, across every system involved — a distinct question from what that identity is then allowed to do, which is security and sharing.

questions.q: In the lesson's partner-integration example, which domains does the request immediately raise beyond integration itself?
options: Only development lifecycle and deployment
Identity (how the partner authenticates) and security (what that identity should be allowed to do) and data architecture (does the volume/shape fit the model)
None — it is purely an integration-architecture decision
Only solution architecture, since it's a cross-cutting practice
questions.explain: Letting an external partner create records directly raises an identity question (how they authenticate), a security question (what they should be allowed to do under least privilege), and a data-architecture question (whether the object model fits their data) — not just an integration question.

questions.q: How does this lesson describe solution architecture relative to the other five domains?
options: It's identical to data architecture under a different name
It's a standalone technical domain with its own object model and APIs
It's less a standalone technical domain and more the practice of weighing trade-offs across all the other domains for one specific solution
It only applies to integration projects
questions.explain: Solution architecture sits differently from the other five domains — it's the cross-cutting practice of balancing trade-offs across all of them for a given solution, which is why Chapter 4 treats it as its own lesson rather than grouping it with the domain deep dives.

questions.q: What does this lesson say actually differentiates an architect from a very senior developer or admin?
options: Knowing more about any single domain than every specialist in that domain
Being able to see across all the domains at once and catch where a good decision in one quietly breaks another
Having the most Trailhead badges
Writing the most Apex code per sprint
questions.explain: The architect usually doesn't out-know a dedicated specialist in that specialist's own domain — the differentiator is being the person in the room who can hold all the domains in view at once and catch where they conflict.
